thread:
jordan (Acme): hitting weird rerank results after upgrading py-sdk to 0.15.0. Top candidate ends up low ranked, scores look off. original behavior with curl was fine. Anyone seen this?
benji (Support): sorry about that — can you paste the request payload you used and a minimal repro?
jordan (Acme): sure, here's a minimal call we make with the python client:
```python
from redwood import Client
import os
client = Client(api_key=os.getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
resp = client.rerank(
    query="how to reset password",
    candidates=["Reset password flow", "Account settings", "Contact support"])
print(resp)
```
benji (Support): can you paste the raw response you get from the SDK (printed resp)?
jordan (Acme): printed resp shows top score mapped to "Account settings" while UI should prefer "Reset password flow". here's the SDK response snippet we log:
```json
{"results": ["Account settings", "Reset password flow", "Contact support"], "scores": ["0.842","0.431","0.120"]}
```
sophiar (Eng): curious — can you run curl with the same payload against the rerank endpoint and paste that response? Also confirm exact py-sdk version.
jordan (Acme): ran curl with identical JSON and got expected order: ["Reset password flow","Account settings","Contact support"] with scores [0.842,0.431,0.120]. py-sdk==0.15.0. weirdly tcpdump of the SDK request shows this payload:
```json
{"query":"how to reset password","candidates":{"1":"Account settings","0":"Reset password flow","2":"Contact support"}}
```
benji (Support): oh — candidates were sent as an object keyed by index, not as a list. that will mess up mapping between candidates and scores on the client side.
sophiar (Eng): confirmed regression — in 0.15.0 we changed internal candidate normalization and accidentally convert the list to {i: candidate} when merging optional metadata. reproduces locally. PR #789 opened to stop dictifying lists. workaround: pin back to 0.14.2 or send raw JSON via client._request_raw. will ship 0.15.1 with hotfix in ~2 hours.
jordan (Acme): downgraded to 0.14.2 — behaviour back to normal, thanks.
ci-bot: created support ticket SUP-45678 for tracking.
sophiar (Eng): pushing hotfix to pypi now, posting release notes once done.
jordan (Acme): :thumbsup: appreciate the fast turnaround.
benji (Support): marking this thread for follow-up; will re-open if you see anything after 0.15.1 update.
